title: PyTorch model files execute code on load: pickle opcode injection
summary: PyTorch model files are ZIP archives of pickled tensors; torch.load() executes pickle opcodes (REDUCE with os.system, GLOBAL with subprocess.Popen, eval/exec) during deserialization, so a tampered model.pth is RCE on load. Unsafe deserialization formats: pickle, torch, joblib, dill, H5/HDF5, ONNX, TorchScript. Treat model artifacts as executable code, not data.

title: nullifAI: container-level scanner evasion via parser disagreement
summary: Malicious HF models re-packed a malicious PyTorch archive inside a 7z container: Picklescan's archive walker did not recognize 7z magic bytes and skipped the file, while torch.load() still read the inner malicious pickle. Any mismatch between a scanner's file parser and the consumer's loader is an exploit seam; HF fixed by teaching Picklescan to scan 7z-packed archives.

title: Malware hidden inside ML model files on PyPI: aliyun-ai-labs SDK campaign
summary: Three fake Aliyun AI Labs SDK packages (aliyun-ai-labs-snippets-sdk, ai-labs-snippets-sdk, aliyun-ai-labs-sdk) shipped a functional infostealer inside a PyTorch model file loaded from __init__.py at import time; ~1,600 downloads in <24h. Model files are treated as data by legacy SCA tools, so they bypass source-only scanning. Zero-trust boundary: model files need their own threat hunting.

title: HF configuration files are a code-execution vector (ConfigScan three attack scenarios)
summary: Model repo config files carry three attack classes: file-operation keys (read/write arbitrary files), website-operation keys (fetch URLs -> SSRF/IP disclosure), and repository-operation keys (_name_or_path redirects model loads to attacker repos -> poisoned weights). Rule-based scan found 13,091/1,324/35,761 suspicious repos per class on HF; LLM-assisted ConfigScan triage cut false positives and found 2 new malicious repos (RagRetriever clones).

title: Pickle deny-list scanning is structurally incomplete; format policy beats opcode scanning
summary: Deny-list scanners (Picklescan) must predict dangerous callables but ML workloads legitimately call thousands from torch/numpy/transformers; allow-list loaders (PyTorch weights_only) reject ~15% of benign pickle repos (PickleBall). 2025 state: require safetensors, refuse pickle at ingress, verify Sigstore signatures via OpenSSF Model Signing v1.0 (April 2025, NVIDIA/HiddenLayer).

title: ML artifact detection toolchain: Picklescan, ModelScan, Fickling, taint analysis, ML-BOM
summary: Tooling state: Picklescan (opcode deny-list, integrated in HF), ModelScan (multi-format), Fickling (pickle decompiler/rewriter), RL Spectra Assure THPs (TH19101/19103 serialized-data-exec, TH16103 base64 dynamic exec), MalHug (dataset loading-script extraction + taint analysis; deployed on an Ant Group HF mirror: 91 malicious models + 9 malicious dataset loaders of 705K models). All are filters, not proof — none do full semantic analysis. ML-BOM (CycloneDX) gives model inventory visibility.

title: CVE-2025-11201: MLflow unauthenticated traversal -> arbitrary file write -> RCE
summary: MLflow Tracking Server /mlflow/model-versions/create accepts an unvalidated 'source' param: traversal sequences (../, ..%2f, ..%5c) escape the artifact store and write arbitrary files (e.g., .py/.pth into sys.path dirs) -> unauthenticated RCE as the MLflow service account. Fix: MLFLOW_CREATE_MODEL_VERSION_SOURCE_VALIDATION_REGEX env var. Hunting signals: traversal in model-version API params, files outside artifact dirs, anomalous writes by mlflow service account. Registry is a first-class RCE surface.

title: CVE-2025-15379: MLflow deploy-time command injection via python_env.yaml
freshness_note: published 2026-04-02; superseded-risk: verify 2.x backport/2026 MLflow status
summary: MLflow with env_manager=LOCAL interpolates dependency strings from a model artifact's python_env.yaml into a shell command without escaping -> a malicious model artifact yields command execution on any system that deploys it. Fixed in 3.8.2 (shlex escaping); NOT backported to 2.x (issue #22429), so 2.x remains vulnerable. Hunting signals: shell metacharacters (;, |, $(), backticks) in python_env.yaml; unexpected process spawns from serving containers.

title: Loader-wrapper deserialization: MLflow pyfunc reintroduces pickle RCE (GHSA-wf7f-8fxf-xfxc)
freshness_note: issue #21083 created 2026-02-23 (file said 02-24); closed 2026-02-25 - verify fix in MLflow 3.10.x+
summary: mlflow.pyfunc.load_model() did not propagate PyTorch weights_only=True to torch.load(), keeping a pickle-RCE path alive via model artifacts even after PyTorch hardened its own API; confirmed on Databricks Runtime 17.4.0 / MLflow 2.20.4. Audit every wrapper loader's deserialization defaults, not just the framework's own API.

title: Model registry as supply-chain choke point: registry write -> deploy-time exec
summary: Registering one malicious artifact (or tampering a model version's source) makes every downstream serve/score/deploy path execute it. Target-selection for ML-infra engagements: exposed MLflow/registry UIs, /mlflow/* REST endpoints, unauthenticated model-version create APIs. Chain: registry write -> deploy-time execution -> ML infrastructure compromise (training data, weights integrity).

title: DeepSeek typosquatting: dormant-account infostealer with legit-platform C2
summary: deepseeek/deepseekai (0.0.8) impersonated DeepSeek API clients on PyPI: account created June 2023 with zero prior activity, payload fired on CLI invocation and stole env vars (API keys, DB creds, cloud permissions), exfiltrated to a Pipedream C2 URL; ~222 downloads before takedown. Code showed AI-assistant authorship markers. Trend-riding (DeepSeek hype) + dormant-account publishing are the tell.

title: AI/ML-themed PyPI malicious package wave: stats and install-time execution
summary: Early 2025: 500+ malicious packages removed from PyPI; ~30% AI/ML-themed (fake transformers/pytorch/tensorflow variants, helper/quantization utils); primary payload credential theft (HF tokens, cloud creds, SSH keys, W&B/MLflow creds). setup.py runs at install time before first import; some packages hide payloads in 'data files' (images/weights/configs) extracted by setup to bypass source static analysis. Exposure window between upload and removal: hours to days.

title: Typosquatting hunting heuristics for package registries
summary: Hunt signals: dormant accounts suddenly publishing; near-name variants of trending packages; low version numbers (0.0.8); download count vs. age mismatch; C2 on legitimate platforms (Pipedream) to dodge infrastructure blocking; AI-generated code (characteristic explanatory comments). Apply to both PyPI and HF hub (models, datasets, orgs).

title: HF hub typosquatting at scale: models, datasets, and organizations
summary: Across 1M+ HF models: 1,574 squatting models vs top-100 downloaded (10.4% malicious), 625 squatting datasets (42.2% impersonation), 302 squatting orgs (4.8% explicit malicious intent). HF is structurally more exposed than PyPI/GitHub: automation-driven workflows load models without manual review; malicious models referencing typosquatted datasets amplify across the dependency chain.

title: Hardcoded HF tokens with write permissions enable org-wide model supply chain compromise
summary: LLaVA-NeXT leaked a hardcoded HuggingFace token with privileged permissions: remote unauthenticated attacker could push/modify models under HF orgs llms-lab, LongVa, Evo-LMM. Tenable advised treating all artifacts of affected orgs as untrusted. Hunting: regex-scan repos for hf_[A-Za-z0-9]+ tokens, verify token permission scopes and org membership; treat write-scoped HF tokens as RCE-equivalent.

title: COLLAPOIS: collaborative backdoor poisoning works with 0.5% compromised clients
summary: Distribute one pre-trained trojaned model to a few compromised FL clients; their coordinated gradients pull the global model toward the trojan's low-loss region. With ~0.5% compromised clients it backdoored 15% of benign clients at 70%+ success under robust FL training, because non-IID scattered benign gradients mask the attack. More client data diversity = fewer clients needed + more stealth.

title: Adaptive FL backdoors defeat OOD/anomaly defenses; detection moved to behavior consistency
summary: 3DFed (decoy updates), DarkFed (cosine constraints), LGA (layer-wise gradient alignment to previous global update) make malicious updates statistically indistinguishable from benign ones, breaking round-level anomaly/OOD detection. 2025 defenses (MARS backdoor energy, FeRA representation-variance consistency + MAD norm-inflation filter, SPMC marginal contribution) detect via cross-round behavioral consistency and per-layer norm distributions instead of fixed statistical rules.

title: Sandboxed artifact loading as evidence discipline for ML findings
summary: Evidence for model-artifact findings must come from containerized loads with strace/network capture; never load untrusted pickles on the host. Zero-trust boundary for all model files entering a dev environment: refuse pickle-format artifacts at ingress unless policy-waivered and signature-verified; keep an ML-BOM of models in the environment.
